target.title: feat(kimi): show code quota in usage status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Kimi Coding subscription users currently do not see quota usage in OpenClaw status surfaces. This adds Kimi quota reporting to the existing provider usage/status pipeline so `5h` and `7d` windows can be shown instead of omitting Kimi.

## Why This Change Was Made

The useful quota data is provider-specific (`/coding/v1/usages`), so the Kimi provider plugin owns the endpoint request and payload normalization while core only owns provider-id routing, summary fan-out, timeout/filtering, and status display.

This rebased version intentionally keeps the surface narrow:

- Registers `kimi` as a usage provider and maps `kimi-code` / `kimi-coding` aliases to it.
- Keeps Kimi endpoint fetch/parsing inside `extensions/kimi-coding/usage.ts` via `resolveUsageAuth` and `fetchUsageSnapshot`.
- Reuses existing Kimi auth sources (`KIMI_API_KEY`, `KIMICODE_API_KEY`, config/store resolution) instead of adding a new env precedence path.
- Does not export a provider-specific Kimi fetch helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-usage`.

## User Impact

When a Kimi API key is available from provider config/store or existing Kimi env vars, OpenClaw can fetch the Kimi Coding usage payload and display:

- `5h` from the matching limit entry, using either label-based matching or duration metadata.
- `7d` from the top-level `usage` row.

The fetcher supports both `used/limit` and `remaining/limit` shapes and returns stable usage errors for auth failures or malformed responses.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof was run on this PR branch before the conflict-only rebase at commit `2873d69d`, using the real local OpenClaw config at `/Users/alex/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, provider `kimi-coding` base URL `https://api.kimi.com/coding/`, and a real Kimi Coding API key resolved from local auth. Token redacted.

Exact live command path: a local Node command with `node --import tsx` imported this PR's `./extensions/kimi-coding/usage.ts`, resolved Kimi usage auth through `resolveProviderAuths({ providers: ["kimi"] })`, and called `fetchKimiUsage(token, 10000, fetch, { baseUrl })` against the real Kimi Coding usage endpoint.

Live endpoint output after this patch:

```json
{
  "proof": "real Kimi Coding usage endpoint via plugin-owned fetchKimiUsage",
  "startedAt": "2026-07-04T10:54:19.421Z",
  "finishedAt": "2026-07-04T10:54:19.572Z",
  "baseUrl": "https://api.kimi.com/coding/",
  "provider": "kimi",
  "displayName": "Kimi",
  "windows": [
    {
      "label": "5h",
      "usedPercent": 0
    },
    {
      "label": "7d",
      "usedPercent": 6
    }
  ],
  "error": null,
  "token": "<redacted>"
}
```

Post-rebase validation on commit `f6be87d3ba`:

- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/kimi-coding/index.test.ts extensions/kimi-coding/usage.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.shared.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/kimi-coding/index.test.ts extensions/kimi-coding/index.ts extensions/kimi-coding/usage.test.ts extensions/kimi-coding/usage.ts src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.ts src/infra/provider-usage.shared.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.shared.ts src/infra/provider-usage.types.ts`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`

What was not tested: full UI rendering was not exercised; this proof covers the live provider usage fetch path and parsed snapshot used by status/usage surfaces.

Related: follow-up to #67593; replaces the broader earlier Kimi/Moonshot usage direction from #20343 with a narrower plugin-owned Kimi Coding integration.
